source_title: The Marshmallow Was Always A Trust Test
summary: This Game Theory classroom source is already public Education evidence: Jiang recasts delayed gratification, resilience, and self-assessment as trust-world effects rather than isolated success traits, then connects class parenting, school formation, social mobility, and revolution as one game.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The marshmallow test is not finally about willpower; waiting becomes rational only when the child trusts that adults keep promises.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Education page already promotes this as a durable lens point, and the episode read already links the exact marshmallow mark to it; this impact pass records that completed routing.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Rich children and poor children learn different games before school: one game rewards negotiation and explanation, while the other often rewards obedience to dangerous authority.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This source supports the broader Education formation anchor by showing that school traits are downstream of the social game a child has already been trained to survive.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the trust-before-self-control spine where success traits become rational only inside a believable world of adult promise, help after failure, and safe self-reflection.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education owns this because the active mechanism is formation through trust, authority, and school-success traits. Human Heart may later use trust relationally, but this source's pressure is institutional and class-formation rather than intimate repair.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the rich-parent / poor-parent contrast as a compact example of class-specific rationality: commands, obedience, negotiation, vocabulary, and teacher relation are not isolated parenting virtues but strategies fitted to different games.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Meritocracy gets nearby class-reproduction pressure only when the active mechanism is wound-to-credential conversion. This source belongs in Education because the child is being trained to inhabit different school and authority games.

new_lens_seeds.title: Game Reset After Mobility Closes
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: When a social game lets a small winning group fill the top positions and reserve them for its children, blocked players eventually stop trying to climb and try to break the game itself.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare dynastic cycles, exam corruption, revolution, elite closure, and mobility collapse, but this source alone routes it as Education/Game Theory pressure rather than a public child page.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Do not create a standalone game-reset page from this source alone. Reopen only if multiple dated sources connect mobility closure, elite inheritance, and revolution as a recurring mechanism outside the Education parent.

chronology_notes.note: This January 13, 2026 source comes after the 2014 Sinica test/trust interview and before later Education compression work; it supplies the classroom formulation that turns marshmallow waiting, resilience, and self-reflection into trust-world effects.

The lecture preserves a strong anti-meritocratic self-example: Jiang says his own route out of poverty required leaving community, taking risks, and lucking into Yale rather than proving that hard work alone is sufficient.

The end of the lecture ties school inequality to Jiang's larger revolution model: social mobility stabilizes a society, but elite inheritance and closed ladders push blocked players toward game reset.
